subject: Dedicated reservation architecture: baseline footprint, min GPUs & geo-burst options
messages:
From: Jake Coleman <jake@lucidpath.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reserve inquiry: production forecast + geo-burst ask

Hi Dev / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — LucidPath is ramping a new multi-tenant assistant product and we need clarity on dedicated reservation options that match our growth plan. High level:
- Peak QPS: ~220 requests/sec across our US region at launch, expected to grow to ~700 qps in 6 months.
- Typical prompt size: 350–800 tokens (including system + user).
- Average response length: ~280 tokens.
- Concurrency pattern: 70% of traffic concentrated in 09:00–18:00 PT weekdays, with unpredictable spikes from campaign-driven events.
- SLA target: 95th p50 latency under 300ms for short prompts; tail behavior acceptable with fallback.

Primary asks:
1) Recommended baseline cluster sizes and min-GPU guarantees for three ramp phases (launch, growth, steady).
2) Practical ramp schedule (weeks to add GPUs, warm-up requirements).
3) Geo-burst strategy for APAC traffic spikes (we'd prefer a small standby in APAC vs multi-region main fleet).
4) Any suggested model/quantization variants to reduce GPU footprint while preserving quality.

Attached is an inference profile export with sample traffic and prompt mix (lucidpath-inference-profile.csv).

Procurement will also want committed minimums for pricing — looping them in.

Appreciate an outline we can bring to our architecture and procurement teams.

Thanks,
Jake Coleman
Head of Platform Engineering — LucidPath
attachments: lucidpath-inference-profile.csv
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Jake Coleman <jake@lucidpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve inquiry: production forecast + geo-burst ask

Hi Jake — thanks for the profile and clear asks. Below is a proposed set of reservation architectures tailored to your traffic profile. I kept options modular so procurement can pick a lane and we can map an activation timeline. See attached PDF for compact pricing and a heatmap (reserve-options-20280910.pdf).

Summary of options (technical):

Option A — Fast Onramp (low upfront)
- Baseline cluster: 8 GPUs (A100-class equivalent) in US region.
- Minimum guaranteed (reserved baseline): 4 GPUs active at all times.
- Burst capacity: up to 24 GPUs via reserved burst lanes + spillover to shared capacity.
- Ramp: 0 -> 8 GPUs day 0; add 8 GPUs at week 4; add final 8 GPUs at week 8 if throughput triggers met.
- Warm-up: suggested 48–72 hour warm-cache window for each + prefix/KV priming during activation.

Option B — Staggered Baseline (balanced reliability/cost)
- Baseline cluster: 16 GPUs in US.
- Minimum guaranteed: 8 GPUs.
- Burst: elastic burst to 40 GPUs with canary pool.
- Ramp: phased (8 GPUs day 0; +8 at week 6; further increases by demand).
- Geo-burst: maintain a 4-GPU warm standby in APAC that can autoscale to 12 GPUs on 15-minute policy.

Option C — Anchored SLA (high throughput, predictable latency)
- Baseline cluster: 32 GPUs across two AZs in US.
- Minimum guaranteed: 20 GPUs.
- Burst: reserve additional 40 GPUs for scheduled bursts (campaigns).
- Ramp: pre-book 50% of final footprint before launch, remainder in month 2–3.
- Warm-up: staged canary and full-warm periods; recommend 2-week soak testing.

Model & runtime optimizations included across options:
- Recommend a 7b quantized variant for high-concurrency interactive paths and a 13b float16 variant for high-quality paths — routing by request profile.
- Prefix caching for repeated system prompts and KV cache reuse for multi-turn sessions.
- Continuous batching with max token cap tuned to 1024 to keep tail latency predictable.

Geo-burst notes:
- Small APAC warm standby (4 GPUs) gives <5 min activation to acceptable capacity for initial spikes and reduces cross-region latency for regional users.
- For stronger regional SLAs, we recommend a second anchored cluster (Option A/B style) in APAC.

Operational considerations:
- Auto-fallback policy: route to quantized model when burst thresholds reached.
- Canary policy: progressive traffic ramp (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) for any model/cluster activation.

Next steps: Marissa can propose the commercial lanes; if you confirm a preferred option we’ll produce an activation schedule and an MOU/term sheet.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: reserve-options-20280910.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jake Coleman <jake@lucidpath.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve inquiry: production forecast + geo-burst ask

Jake — looping commercial context.

Quick commercial framing based on Dev's technical lanes:
- Option A (Fast Onramp): 3-month minimum term, monthly invoiced reservation for reserved baseline GPUs. Reserved GPU unit price: $5,500 / GPU / month (example; final pricing to be in term sheet).
- Option B (Staggered Baseline): 6–12 month term recommended; step-down credit for unused reserved units after month 3 subject to review.
- Option C (Anchored SLA): 12 month term; we include SLA credits for availability and a dedicated support/response SLA.

Minimum commitment asks from procurement we typically see: 4–8 GPUs reserved to start for smaller pilots; enterprise customers often commit to a 10–20 GPU baseline for production. For your profile, Option B with an 8 GPU minimum looks like the highest ROI entry.

We can also include pilot credits to help with initial warm-up. Sean (CS) — please prepare a short onboarding checklist for the APAC standby activation and rate-limit rules so procurement has expected ops overhead.

If LucidPath is ready to move, we'll issue an MOU and proposed SOW; Dev, can you attach the SOW template to the MOU?

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks all. A few procurement and security clarifications before we proceed:
1) SOC 2 Type II evidence and subprocessor list — can you provide a copy or redacted SOC 2 report?
2) Network egress policy: can we define VPC peering and egress IP ranges for allowlisting? Can APAC standby be limited to specific subnets?
3) Do you support an on-prem/private deployment option (customer managed) if regulatory needs require it?
4) We need an initial SOW (technical scope + deliverables + timeline) and draft MSA for our legal team to review.

Attached is our procurement questionnaire and a high-level SOW template for your input (lucidpath-procurement-questions.pdf).

Regards,
LucidPath Procurement
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve inquiry: production forecast + geo-burst ask

Hi — quick answers and next steps.

1) SOC 2: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and the current subprocessor list within 48 business hours. I will attach the redacted report to the MOU packet.
2) Network: VPC peering and static egress ranges are supported in our Dedicated + Private offerings. APAC standby can be scoped to a constrained subnet; we will document CIDR ranges in the SOW.
3) Private deployment: yes — Redwood Private is an option; we can include on-prem deployment scoping as an add-on in the SOW.
4) SOW & MSA: Marissa will circulate a draft MOU/SOW. For timeline, if LucidPath signs MOU by 09/20 we can provision baseline reserved capacity within 10 business days and follow the Option B ramp cadence to reach the nominated footprint within 8–10 weeks.
